text:
Nashville arrives on a four-game winning streak, the latest a 3-1 home win over STL three days ago. Los Angeles comes in 2-3-0 over its last five after a 5-2 home loss to PIT, and it is without Erik Gustafsson. There is a human side too: Erik Haula faces the Predators for the first time since leaving them, after 132 games in their colours.

Our numbers see little to separate them. At five on five, NSH has taken 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and LAK 50%, and our model projects 3.12 goals for LAK to 2.87 for NSH. LAK has also taken 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. In net, projected starter Juuse Saros is at +6.3 goals saved above expected this season, while Anton Forsberg is at -0.8, though Forsberg was at +8.5 last year when Saros was at -10.2.

Steven Stamkos is our top scoring pick for NSH at 36%, and he had two points against STL, as CBS Sports noted. Roman Josi sits one point from 800 career points. For LAK, Adrian Kempe leads at 38% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Quinton Byfield, at 50% for a point, above his season pace of 43%, because his line creates chances (4.01 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice). He is a player to watch, not a lock.
